clue.text: Can a tart love short-tempered actor?

parts.note: can is slang for a lavatory, as is john in American English

indicators.note: tempered metal is worked and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged
short means the word love is cut, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Would a sharp-tongued, quick-tempered actor manage to love a tart?
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts LOVE to LOV, and 'tempered' rearranges A TART LOV into TRAVOLTA.
explanation.definitionFit: The American film star of Grease and Saturday Night Fever is a well-known example of an actor.

clue.text: Form of transport initially discovered in Pharaoh's time

definitions.text: Form of transport initially discovered in Pharaoh's time

parts.words: Form of transport initially discovered in Pharaoh's time
parts.note: the initials of this train, H S T, are found inside the words Pharaoh's time, which is the sense of initially discovered in

explanation.surface: An archaeologist claims a kind of transport was first found in ancient Egyptian times.
explanation.walkthrough: HST is the usual British abbreviation for this kind of fast train, and those three letters sit across 'PharaoH'S Time'. 'initially' tells you the hidden run is the answer's initials, not the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast passenger rail service is a form of transport, in Britain usually called by its initials HST.

clue.text: 18th-century politician in conflict over northern battle

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict
re means about, concerning, the sense of over in 'argue over'
the Battle of Hastings, 1066, when the Normans conquered England

explanation.surface: An eighteenth-century politician argued about a battle in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: He was the first Governor-General of British India, famously impeached at Westminster.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Governor-General of Bengal was a British statesman of the 1700s, impeached in a long trial.

clue.text: Very inexperienced new SAS soldier initially rages with anger

indicators.note: new tells you the following letters are made into a fresh arrangement
initially means take only the first letter of soldier

explanation.surface: A raw new recruit to the SAS flies into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SAS, S (from 'initially' on 'soldier'), RAGES and ANGER into the fourteen letters of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone as green as grass is extremely naive, green being an old idiom for untried and immature.

clue.text: Chinaman treating a crofter — do boots briefly get taken off?

indicators.note: treating, as in processing or working on, signals that the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: briefly means the word boots is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A Chinese doctor treats a Highland smallholder: does he have to take his boots off?
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims BOOTS to BOOT, and 'treating' rearranges A CROFTER DO BOOT. A crofter farms a small rented holding in the Scottish Highlands. The definition word is now considered dated and offensive; the setter later said he had not known that.
explanation.definitionFit: These were part-trained rural health workers in Mao's China, so one such worker was a Chinese man or woman.

clue.text: Gather it's more flipping valuable, perhaps

parts.note: to gather things is to collect them

indicators.note: flipping, as in tossing over and over, signals the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone collects things whose resale price keeps rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' rearranges IT'S MORE into ORSITEM. 'flipping' also works in the surface as a mild British intensifier.
explanation.definitionFit: An object prized by enthusiasts is often worth money, hence the hedge 'perhaps' on valuable.

clue.text: Endlessly horny maneater cast as gross-out? On the contrary

definitions.note: the definition is the reverse of gross-out, that is outgross, a verb

indicators.note: cast, as metal is recast in a mould, signals the letters are reshaped
endlessly means the word horny loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A randy man-eating predator plays a role in a crude comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the Y and 'cast' shuffles the rest. 'On the contrary' turns gross-out round to outgross: to take more at the box office. Gross-out is a crude comedy genre.
explanation.definitionFit: To outgross a rival film is to surpass it in takings, which is exactly what the phrase says.

clue.text: Cuts China off in seconds

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the seconds

parts.note: mo is a moment, so seconds gives mos

indicators.note: off, as in gone wrong, tells you the letters of China are disordered

explanation.surface: Beijing is cut off within seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' disorders the letters of China, and 'in' places them inside the seconds. 'Cuts' looks like a verb but names hairstyles.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohicans are haircuts with a central strip of hair and the sides shaved, named after the Native American people.

clue.text: A killer said to carry a jacket full of useless facts and figures?

definitions.text: jacket full of useless facts and figures?
definitions.note: both a hooded weatherproof jacket and a person obsessed with trivia

indicators.note: to carry means the first piece holds the second inside it
said means the words are heard, not spelt, so an orc becomes an ork

parts.note: an orc is a killer whale, or a murderous goblin of fantasy

explanation.surface: A murderer was reportedly carrying a jacket stuffed with trivia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns AN ORC into AN ORK, and 'to carry' puts A inside it before the K. The definition plays on both senses: the hooded coat, and the trainspotting type stereotypically wearing one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded waterproof coat, and by extension the nerdy enthusiast who wears one and hoards trivia.

clue.text: Bit of a bloomer from Top Cat

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the cat loses its first letter

parts.note: a panther is a big cat

explanation.surface: Part of a gaffe comes from a cartoon cat.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Cat is a cartoon alley cat, but here 'Top' is a verb removing the head of PANTHER. 'bloomer' is a flower, not a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollen-bearing part of a stamen is a piece of a flower, here called a bloomer.

clue.text: Redbreast by Scott, say?

parts.note: tit is slang for a breast
Scott spoken sounds like Scot, and Ian is the crossword's stock Scottish man

explanation.surface: A robin, painted by Peter Scott perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Peter Scott was a bird painter, so the surface pictures a robin portrait. 'say' marks Scott as heard: a Scot, typically IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian is a reddish-auburn hair colour, named after the Venetian painter's favoured shade.

clue.text: Drink? Right, that is a drink

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
a sling is a spirit-based cocktail, as in Singapore sling

explanation.surface: Fancy a drink? Yes, that one's a drink all right.
explanation.definitionFit: A white wine from the German grape of that name is one kind of drink.

clue.text: Beastly pair some would say solvers were familiar with?

indicators.note: some would say points to how the words sound when spoken, not how they are spelt

parts.note: the solvers addressed are you, and were familiar with means knew

explanation.surface: Solvers would claim they already knew this pair of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: A deliberately silly clue: 'you knew' and the two animals sound alike, at least in most accents.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep and an African antelope make a pair of animals, that is, beasts.

clue.text: Manages boards

definitions.meaning: climbs aboard a bus or train

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both coping (getting along) and climbing aboard, as onto a train.

clue.text: See 13
See 2
Female cut by whip at boarding school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English boarding school
a crop is a short riding whip

explanation.surface: A girl is lashed at a boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is an elite English boys' boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A very short sleek haircut fashionable among women in the 1920s, hence a female hairstyle.

clue.text: Day in which banker gets backed in the City

indicators.note: backed means the whole assembly is read from the back
in which says the day holds the banker inside it

parts.note: Thu is the abbreviation for Thursday
a banker in betting is a certainty, a cert

explanation.surface: A day when a financier gets support in the Square Mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' gives TH(CERT)U, and 'backed' turns it round. 'banker' and 'backed' are racing slang: a cert is a sure bet. The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Utrecht is a city in the central Netherlands.

clue.text: See 1
See 3
Bent over page in dictionary with two consecutive letters at beginning

indicators.note: at beginning puts the consecutive letters at the front of the rest

parts.note: S and T follow one another in the alphabet

indicators.note: in says the over and page letters go inside the dictionary

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone leaned over a page of a dictionary with two letters at its start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts over and page inside the dictionary, and 'at beginning' sets the two letters in front. 'Bent over' looks like the definition, but 'over' is needed for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Stooped describes a body bent forward, as in an elderly person's posture.

clue.text: See 26
See 4
Model in US cut record, first of several items on display

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
ax is the American spelling of axe, to cut
a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of several is taken

explanation.surface: An American model's cut record was the first of several on show.
explanation.walkthrough: Until 2014 British motorists had to show a paper tax disc on the windscreen as proof of paying road tax.
explanation.definitionFit: These paper circles were displayed in car windscreens, so they were items on display.

clue.text: Want a Dylan album?

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a craving, and is also the title of Bob Dylan's 1976 record.

clue.text: See 5
See 11
Garden? Try one of the other two when disheartened

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try

indicators.note: disheartened means the name loses a letter from its heart

parts.note: Bill Oddie was one of Graeme Garden's two fellow ...

explanation.surface: Advice to a gardener: try one of the other two plots when feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goodies were a British comedy trio of the 1970s: Graeme Garden, Tim Brooke-Taylor and Bill Oddie. 'disheartened' removes a middle D from ODDIE, giving ODIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Graeme Garden was a member of the comedy trio, so he is one example of the group's members.

clue.text: One seeking favour from escort, around start of tour

indicators.note: around says the escort goes round the next letter

parts.note: a courier escorts and guides tourists

indicators.note: start of means take only the first letter of tour

explanation.surface: A guide around the start of a tour is after a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' gives T from 'tour', and 'around' puts COURIER round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal attendant is stereotypically a flatterer seeking advancement, so one seeking favour.

clue.text: Flowery stuff? Just a little in the Czech Republic

indicators.note: in places the trace inside the country code

parts.note: CZ is the international vehicle code for the Czech Republic
a hint is just a trace

explanation.surface: Is there a flowery fabric in the Czech Republic? Only a trace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the trace inside the country code. 'stuff' is an old word for fabric, so 'Flowery stuff' is floral cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: This glazed cotton fabric is typically printed with floral patterns, so flowery material.

clue.text: See 6
See 7
Musician capturing essential character of first violin part?

indicators.note: capturing means the musician holds another letter inside

parts.note: Sting is the English singer and bass player

indicators.note: the essential character is the middle letter of the word first

explanation.surface: A musician captures the essence of a first violin part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential character of' gives R, the middle of 'first', and 'capturing' puts STING round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin has four strings, so one of them is a part of the instrument.

clue.text: US shopkeeper rushed male into hospital

indicators.note: into puts the rushed male inside the hospital

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium
tore means rushed, as in tore down the road

explanation.surface: An American shopkeeper rushed a man into hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts the rushed male inside the hospital. San, short for sanatorium, is a crossword staple for a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a person who runs a store is a shopkeeper.
